clusters.summary: The grafana-cli accessor re-implements the token fallback with no feature-toggle check, so the CLI uses a different credential than the server
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the CLI accessor prefers proxy_token with no flag check, and grep shows zero openfeature refs under pkg/cmd/grafana-cli. The toggle does not gate the CLI path the docs claim it gates.

clusters.summary: The docs name the toggle without its registered grafana. prefix, so following them does not enable the feature
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: ReadFeatureTogglesFromInitFile keys flags verbatim by ini key name, so enabling the undotted 'dedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken' the docs name does not enable grafana.dedicated... at setting.go:763.

clusters.summary: GcomToken() has no production caller after the migration but is retained on the interface, impl and mock
clusters.rationale: Verified by grep: GcomToken survives only on the interface, impl and mock, with no production caller. Two near-identical accessors with Gcom/GrafanaCom naming drift — cleanup, not a bug.

clusters.summary: defaults.ini gained proxy_token but sample.ini, the template operators copy, was not updated
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the [grafana_com] block in sample.ini still lists only url, api_url, sso_api_token, and contribute/create-pull-request.md:138-141 requires both files change together.

clusters.summary: The toggle is sampled once at boot but the registry entry omits RequiresRestart: true
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the flag is sampled once at cli.go:113 / target.go:99 and baked into a plain string, yet the entry omits RequiresRestart while 40 siblings in the file set it for exactly this.

clusters.summary: The flag name is a hardcoded string literal instead of the generated featuremgmt constant
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the literal duplicates FlagGrafanaDedicatedGrafanaComProxyAPIToken with no compile-time link, and toggles_gen.json records four renames of this flag in eight days. A fifth silently disables it.

clusters.summary: The resolver discards the OpenFeature evaluation error and logs none of its outcomes, so the token source is unobservable
clusters.rationale: Accurate: the resolver logs nothing and drops the evaluation error, so the chosen token source is unobservable. Real but small — a debug line fixes it; no behavior is wrong.

clusters.summary: Resolve overwrites the parsed proxy_token in place using one field as both input and output, making it destructive and non-idempotent
clusters.rationale: Real: the assignment uses one field as input and output, so the parsed proxy_token is destroyed and a later caller cannot tell whether one was configured. The CLI reads the same field pre-resolution.

clusters.summary: The field and method comments do not disclose the two-phase raw/effective meaning of the field
clusters.rationale: Accurate: the field comment says 'the dedicated auth token' but after resolution the field usually holds the SSO token, and neither comment mentions the raw/effective split. Doc-comment accuracy.

clusters.summary: Resolution is an unenforced lifecycle contract: a bootstrap that skips the call yields an unauthenticated proxy
clusters.rationale: Real: the effective value of a field two consumers now read is produced only by a mutator called from two places, enforced solely by a doc comment. testinfra.go:124 already misses it.

clusters.summary: The integration-test harness initializes OpenFeature but never calls the resolver, so test servers proxy unauthenticated
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: InitOpenFeatureWithCfg is called there but ResolveGrafanaComProxyAPIToken is not, so test servers serving /api/gnet would proxy with no token even when sso_api_token is set.

clusters.summary: The docs scope the token to catalog browsing and CLI installs, but it backs the whole /api/gnet/* proxy
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the same field feeds grafana_com_proxy.go:54 (the whole /api/gnet/* proxy) and pluginconfig/config.go:39, not just catalog browsing and grafana-cli. An operator would mis-scope the token.

clusters.summary: The new doc line uses a Hugo relref shortcode, the only one in the file, against the documented convention
clusters.rationale: Verified: this is the only relref in the file and in the whole setup-grafana tree, and docs/AGENTS.md:110 mandates inline Markdown links. Convention drift.

clusters.summary: The doc link anchor is probably wrong: sibling headings render underscores as dashes
clusters.rationale: Evidence points the other way: in-file anchors #root_url (:269) and #auto_assign_org_role (:960) preserve underscores. #grafana-com at :2310 is itself broken, as is #external-image-store.

clusters.summary: The docs never mention the sso_api_token fallback, the most operationally important behavior
clusters.rationale: Correct: the new doc block never mentions that an unset or toggle-disabled proxy_token silently falls back to sso_api_token. An omission rather than an error.

clusters.summary: The generated toggles JSON permanently records tombstones for phantom flag names
clusters.rationale: Claim is that the tombstones are normal generator output, not a defect. That is correct — the file already carried ~98 such entries.

clusters.summary: A mockery DO NOT EDIT file was hand-edited and will not survive regeneration
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: file header says 'mockery v2.31.4. DO NOT EDIT.', the new block lacks the '// X provides a mock function' comment every generated method has, and no .mockery.yaml or go:generate exists.

clusters.summary: skipStaticRootValidation is set without restoring it
clusters.rationale: Verified: skipStaticRootValidation is already set unconditionally at setting_test.go:30. The new assignment is redundant, not harmful; the claim says exactly that.

clusters.summary: The new grafana_com test is placed among plugin-settings tests and names a function that does not exist
clusters.rationale: Verified by grep: readGrafanaComSettings exists nowhere; the file's convention (Test_readPluginSettings) names a real function. Also a [grafana_com] test sitting in the plugin-settings file.

clusters.summary: Neither the CLI accessor nor the gnet proxy has a test asserting which token reaches the Authorization header
clusters.rationale: Verified: pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/utils has no test files and pkg/api has no grafana_com_proxy_test.go. Nothing asserts which credential reaches the wire — the whole point of the change.

clusters.summary: The only CLI token test still asserts the dead GcomToken(), so the new path is untested
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the only CLI token test asserts c.GcomToken(), which now has zero production callers; the new accessor's fallback logic has no coverage in either branch.

clusters.summary: Dotted flag names cannot be enabled via cfg: overrides because the parser skips any key containing a dot
clusters.rationale: Verified: applyFeatureToggleCmdOverrides continues on any key containing a dot, so cfg:feature_toggles.grafana.dedicated... is a silent no-op. Pre-existing, but this change adds a dotted flag.

clusters.summary: The new test drives the value only by environment variable, so the defaults.ini key is unexercised
clusters.rationale: Technically true — the env second pass at setting.go:906 creates the key regardless — but the defaults.ini line is behaviorally inert (valueAsString already defaults to ""), so a test for it would assert nothing.

clusters.summary: Three byte-identical subtest bodies should be table-driven
clusters.rationale: Correct: three near-identical subtest bodies differing only in inputs, in a file that already uses table style at :441 and :661. Pure style.

clusters.summary: A new subtest is tautological — it passes with the resolver guard removed
clusters.rationale: Accurate: cfg.Load already sets the field to dedicated-token from the env var, so this subtest passes with the function body emptied. It does still catch an unconditional-overwrite mutation.

clusters.summary: setProvider cleanup restores NoopProvider rather than the previously installed provider
clusters.rationale: Correct: the cleanup installs NoopProvider rather than restoring the prior provider, leaving process-global SDK state altered for the rest of the binary. No failure today.

clusters.summary: The plugin repo client attaches the token on an unanchored URL prefix match
clusters.rationale: Correct: strings.HasPrefix is not anchored at a host boundary, and the base URL is operator-supplied via --repo. Real but pre-existing and requires the operator's own misconfiguration to bite.

clusters.summary: applyCommandLineProperties appends cfg: overrides unredacted to the applied-properties log
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: applyCommandLineProperties appends the raw value while its sibling at :1138 uses RedactedValue, and LogConfigSources logs it at Info. cfg:grafana_com.proxy_token=<secret> is printed in clear.

clusters.summary: No audit log records who drove a proxied grafana.com call with the instance credential
clusters.rationale: Accurate — ProxyGnetRequest logs nothing identifying the caller while substituting the instance credential. Entirely pre-existing and an enhancement, not a defect this change introduces.

clusters.summary: The CLI config-parse error is logged at Debug, so an unreadable config produces no output
clusters.rationale: Verified: pkg/cmd/grafana-cli/logger.Debug is gated on debugmode, so a config-parse failure is silent and yields an empty token. Real, but copied verbatim from the pre-existing GcomToken.

clusters.summary: A 176-character line packs client construction, evaluation and the emptiness check together
clusters.rationale: Measured 187 chars (finding said 176), packing client construction, evaluation and the emptiness test with the interesting case as a bare return. Readability only.

clusters.summary: The toggle description implies grafana-cli coverage it does not have and omits that it is inert without proxy_token
clusters.rationale: Fair: the description reads as covering grafana-cli (which never evaluates the flag) and omits that the toggle is inert without proxy_token. Wording only.

clusters.summary: Grafana Enterprise entry points outside this repository would need the same resolver insertion
clusters.rationale: The must-call-after-init requirement lives only in a doc comment, so a downstream Enterprise entry point could miss it. Conditional and unverifiable from this repo, but a fair caution.

clusters.summary: proxy_token is added bare with no comment saying it is inert without the toggle
clusters.rationale: Verified: no key in the [grafana_com] stanza of defaults.ini carries a comment. The new line matches its siblings exactly; the finding's own evidence concedes this.

clusters.summary: The per-setting environment-variable callout is the only one of its kind in the file
clusters.rationale: Verified: the generic GF_ override rule is stated once at lines 79-90 and no other standard key carries a per-setting callout. Harmless redundancy.

clusters.summary: The field name is ambiguous about which credential it holds after resolution
clusters.rationale: The claim as stated is that the name is clear enough and naming is out of scope — i.e. no defect. Nothing actionable.

clusters.summary: openfeature.NewDefaultClient allocates a new client on every call
clusters.rationale: Accurate but inconsequential: one client allocation on a once-per-process boot path, explicitly stated as having no correctness impact.

clusters.summary: There is no strict mode: an operator cannot express "never fall back to the SSO token"
clusters.rationale: True that every negative path falls back to the broader SSO credential with no way to opt out. Correct observation, but the fallback is the stated design intent — a feature request.

clusters.summary: Whether an empty EvaluationContext discards global targeting context
clusters.rationale: Refutation of an empty-EvaluationContext hazard; the SDK merges rather than erases global context. Asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: Whether context.Background() with no timeout can hang startup
clusters.rationale: Verified: CreateHTTPClient defaults to a 10s timeout, so context.Background() cannot hang boot. Claim asserts no defect and is right.

clusters.summary: Whether the new pkg/setting to openfeature edge introduces an import cycle
clusters.rationale: Cleared: pkg/setting already depended on the openfeature module via memprovider, and openfeature is external so no cycle is possible. No defect asserted.

clusters.summary: Whether a runtime config reload could revert or wipe the resolved token
clusters.rationale: Cleared hypothesis: no OSS path re-invokes cfg.Load after startup, so the resolution cannot be reverted. Not a defect report.

clusters.summary: Whether the sso_api_token fallback is backward compatible
clusters.rationale: Claim is that operators on sso_api_token alone are unaffected. True, and it is a clearance rather than a defect report.

clusters.summary: Whether the in-place Cfg mutation is a data race
clusters.rationale: Cleared: both call sites run before any server goroutine holds the Cfg pointer. Claim is explicitly that there is no race today.

clusters.summary: Whether the PROXY_TOKEN$ redaction pattern is correct and complete
clusters.rationale: Claim is that the PROXY_TOKEN$ pattern is correct and its breadth is safe. Both hold; no defect asserted.

clusters.summary: Whether the resolver boolean logic is correct and convergent across flag states
clusters.rationale: Claim is that the boolean logic is correct across all four flag/token combinations. It is. A clearance, not a finding.

clusters.summary: Whether discarding the evaluation error departs from the codebase idiom
clusters.rationale: Claim is that discarding the OpenFeature error matches the codebase-wide idiom. Correct; asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: Whether a whitespace-only proxy_token is accepted and sent
clusters.rationale: Correct: a whitespace-only proxy_token passes the != "" guard, suppressing the SSO fallback and sending 'Bearer  '. The sibling token is TrimSpace'd at backend.go:57. Outcome is a 401.

clusters.summary: Whether the legacy [grafana_net] alias applies to proxy_token
clusters.rationale: Claim is that the [grafana_net] alias never applied to token keys and this is not a regression. Verified: [grafana_net] carries only url. Not a defect report.

clusters.summary: Whether c.Config() re-parses the INI file on every accessor call
clusters.rationale: Claim is that re-parsing the INI per accessor call is a pre-existing, cost-only pattern in a one-shot process. Correct; no defect asserted.

clusters.summary: Whether the CLI logger call is a structured-logger arity bug
clusters.rationale: Verified: the CLI logger's Debug is a variadic fmt.Println wrapper with no key/value contract. The refutation is right; no defect asserted.

clusters.summary: Whether %2e%2e in the gnet wildcard can escape the /api prefix
clusters.rationale: Self-declared unresolved with two unconfirmed steps and no demonstrated defect; the target host stays grafana.com regardless. Honest, but nothing a maintainer can act on as written.

clusters.summary: Whether the token could leak via an HTTP redirect
clusters.rationale: Cleared hypothesis: Go's http.Client strips Authorization on cross-host redirects. No defect asserted.

clusters.summary: Whether the token could leak to a non-grafana.com host via --pluginUrl
clusters.rationale: Verified: Authorization is attached only when the URL is prefixed by the configured grafana.com API URL, so --pluginUrl downloads do not receive it. Asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: Whether an unresolved token field degrades safely at the proxy
clusters.rationale: Verified: the director sets Authorization only when the token is non-empty, so an unresolved field degrades to anonymous. Claim asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: Whether the resolved token could be exposed via /api/admin/settings
clusters.rationale: Cleared hypothesis: admin settings serialize the redacting SettingsProvider, not the Cfg struct. Claim asserts no exposure and is consistent with the redaction path.

clusters.summary: Threat-model note: the change is net-neutral by default
clusters.rationale: A summary that the change is attack-surface-neutral by default. Accurate restatement of what the diff does; no action for a maintainer.

clusters.summary: Whether the registry entry Generate flags deviate from siblings
clusters.rationale: Generate{Go: true} appears 13x in registry.go; an established alternate pattern. Claim says it is not a deviation worth acting on, and that is correct.

clusters.summary: Whether the production entry points sequence OpenFeature init and resolution correctly
clusters.rationale: Clearance: both production entry points call the resolver after OpenFeature init and before Initialize. Verified against the diff; not a defect report.

clusters.summary: Whether the generated toggle files are consistent with the registry entry
clusters.rationale: Clearance: generated toggle files are consistent with the registry entry and the grafana. prefix has precedent. Asserts no defect.

clusters.summary: Whether the mock type assertion panics on nil
clusters.rationale: Verified: the new block is byte-identical in shape to every sibling mock method. Standard mockery contract, no defect claimed.

clusters.summary: Whether the new subtests are mutation-sensitive and can actually fail
clusters.rationale: Mutation claims check out for the three named mutations. This is a clearance, not a defect report, so it carries no action for a maintainer.

clusters.summary: Whether swapping the OpenFeature provider pollutes global state across subtests
clusters.rationale: Claim is that the global provider swap does not pollute other tests. Correct for this package — no parallel subtests and nothing else evaluates flags. Not a defect report.

clusters.summary: The /api/gnet/* route proxies any method and caller-controlled path with the instance credential, guarded only by reqSignedIn
clusters.rationale: Accurate: r.Any + reqSignedIn only, caller-controlled wildcard path, and the director substitutes the instance grafana.com bearer. Pre-existing, but it is the credential this change repoints.

clusters.summary: No test asserts that ProvidePluginManagementConfig or ProxyGnetRequest carry the resolved token
clusters.rationale: Verified: config_test.go contains no token assertion, so the one-line field swap is unguarded. Small and easy to add; narrower than the proxy-level gap.

clusters.summary: No test pins the idempotency / second-call contract of the resolver
clusters.rationale: True that no test pins a second call, but the resolver is invoked exactly once per process; pinning an unreachable contract is not worth a maintainer's attention.

clusters.summary: Recursive dependency install rebuilds the options without carrying the token forward
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the dependency recursion rebuilds pluginInstallOpts with only insecure/repoURL/pluginDir, dropping gcomToken. Dependencies are fetched anonymously after the parent is extracted.

clusters.summary: Whether InitializeForCLI misses the resolver and the grafana-cli runner path is affected
clusters.rationale: Verified by grep: ProvidePluginManagementConfig appears only at wire_gen.go:367 and :1073, so InitializeForCLI is unaffected. Explicitly a dropped claim.

clusters.summary: A test comment names the wrong method for the path now exercised and misattributes behavior
clusters.rationale: Confirmed: the comment names GcomToken() but the exercised path now calls GrafanaComProxyAPIToken(), and baseCommandLine (line 133) supplies both. Stale comment.
